content.title: The Cell: Life's Basic Unit
content.explanation: Your body is made of about 37 trillion cells - tiny living units that do all the work of keeping you alive. Cells eat, breathe, grow, and make copies of themselves. Some organisms like bacteria are just one cell. You started as just ONE cell!
content.visualAlt: Cell diagram showing nucleus and organelles
keyPoints: All living things are made of cells
Cells carry out all life functions
Unicellular = one cell (bacteria), Multicellular = many (humans)
Your body has about 37 trillion cells

content.title: Cell Parts and Their Jobs
content.explanation: Think of a cell like a tiny city. The nucleus is the city hall (controls everything). The mitochondria are the power plants (make energy). The cell membrane is the city wall (controls what enters and exits). Each part has a critical job!
keyPoints: Nucleus: control center, contains DNA
Mitochondria: make energy from food (ATP)
Cell membrane: controls what enters/exits
Ribosomes: make proteins
Vacuole: stores water and waste

content.question: Which organelle is called the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
content.hint: It produces energy (ATP) for the cell from food molecules.
content.explanationOnCorrect: The mitochondria! It converts food (glucose) into ATP energy that powers all cell activities. One cell can have thousands of mitochondria!
content.explanationOnWrong: The mitochondria are the powerhouses. They produce ATP energy from glucose and oxygen.

content.question: True or False: Bacteria are multicellular organisms.
content.hint: How many cells does a bacterium have?
content.explanationOnCorrect: False is correct! Bacteria are unicellular - each bacterium is just one single cell doing everything by itself.
content.explanationOnWrong: Bacteria are unicellular - they consist of just ONE cell. You, however, are multicellular with trillions of cells!

content.question: What is the main job of the cell membrane?
options: Control what enters and exits the cell
correct: Control what enters and exits the cell
content.hint: Think of a city wall or security checkpoint.
content.explanationOnCorrect: The cell membrane is a selective barrier - it lets nutrients in and waste products out, protecting the cell!
content.explanationOnWrong: The membrane acts like a wall with gates - it controls traffic in and out of the cell.

content.title: DNA: The Blueprint of Life
content.explanation: DNA is a long molecule inside every cell's nucleus. It contains instructions for building and running your entire body - like a recipe book with 3 billion 'letters'. DNA is organized into 46 chromosomes. Half came from your mother, half from your father!
keyPoints: DNA = deoxyribonucleic acid
DNA contains genes - instructions for building proteins
Humans have ~3 billion DNA base pairs
DNA is organized into 46 chromosomes (23 pairs)
You inherit 23 chromosomes from each parent

content.title: Photosynthesis: Plants Eat Sunlight
content.explanation: Plants make their own food from sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide. This process is called photosynthesis. The green chemical chlorophyll in leaves captures sunlight and uses that energy to combine CO₂ + water into glucose (sugar) + oxygen. You breathe the oxygen plants release!
content.visualAlt: Plant showing sunlight, CO2 in and O2 out
keyPoints: Equation: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
Chlorophyll (green pigment) captures light energy
Glucose (sugar) stores the energy
Oxygen is released as a byproduct - the air we breathe!

content.question: How many chromosomes do humans normally have?
content.hint: You get 23 from mom + 23 from dad = ?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Correct! 23 from each parent = 46 total, arranged in 23 pairs. These 46 chromosomes contain all your genetic instructions.
content.explanationOnWrong: You receive 23 chromosomes from each parent, totaling 46. They're organized as 23 matching pairs.

content.question: What does a plant release as a byproduct of photosynthesis?
content.hint: Plants take in CO₂ and water. The air we need to breathe comes from somewhere...
content.explanationOnCorrect: Yes! Plants release oxygen as a byproduct. All the oxygen in Earth's atmosphere was produced by plants and algae through photosynthesis!
content.explanationOnWrong: Photosynthesis: CO₂ + H₂O → glucose + OXYGEN. Plants release the oxygen we breathe!

content.question: Fill in the blank: DNA is stored in the ___ of a cell.
content.explanationOnCorrect: Correct! The nucleus houses the cell's DNA, keeping it protected and organized into chromosomes.
content.explanationOnWrong: DNA is kept in the nucleus - the cell's control center. The nucleus protects this precious genetic information.

content.title: The Human Body Systems
content.explanation: Your body has 11 organ systems all working together. The circulatory system pumps blood. The respiratory system breathes. The nervous system controls everything using electrical signals. The digestive system breaks down food into fuel. They all cooperate to keep you alive!
keyPoints: Circulatory: heart + blood vessels deliver oxygen and nutrients
Respiratory: lungs exchange O₂ for CO₂
Nervous: brain + nerves control everything
Digestive: breaks food into nutrients
Immune: defends against disease

content.title: Ecosystems and Food Webs
content.explanation: An ecosystem is a community of living things and their environment. Energy flows through ecosystems in food webs. Plants (producers) use sunlight. Herbivores (primary consumers) eat plants. Carnivores (secondary consumers) eat herbivores. Decomposers recycle everything back to soil!
content.visualAlt: Food web showing producers, consumers, decomposers
keyPoints: Producers: plants make their own food via photosynthesis
Primary consumers: eat plants (rabbits, deer, cows)
Secondary consumers: eat herbivores (foxes, wolves)
Decomposers: break down dead matter (fungi, bacteria)
Energy decreases at each level (only 10% transfers up)

content.question: The circulatory system's main job is to:
options: Deliver oxygen and nutrients to all body cells
correct: Deliver oxygen and nutrients to all body cells
content.hint: Think about what your heart pumps through your blood vessels.
content.explanationOnCorrect: Yes! Your heart pumps blood through a network of vessels, delivering oxygen and nutrients to every cell and removing waste.
content.explanationOnWrong: The circulatory system (heart + blood vessels) transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and removes waste from every cell.

content.question: In a food chain, a deer eating grass makes the deer a:
content.hint: Grass is the producer. The deer eats the producer directly.
content.explanationOnCorrect: Correct! The deer is the first animal in the chain that eats a producer (grass), making it a primary consumer.
content.explanationOnWrong: The grass produces its own food (producer). The deer eats the producer directly = primary consumer.

content.title: Evolution and Natural Selection
content.explanation: Charles Darwin discovered that species change over time through natural selection. Individuals with traits that help them survive and reproduce pass those traits to offspring. Over millions of years, this causes species to change dramatically - even splitting into new species!
keyPoints: Natural selection: best-adapted individuals survive and reproduce
Traits that help survival are passed on more
Over millions of generations, species change
All life on Earth shares a common ancestor

content.question: In a population of mice, darker fur makes them harder for hawks to spot. Over generations, you'd expect:
content.hint: Which mice survive longer to have offspring?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Yes! Dark mice survive more often, reproduce more, and pass on dark fur genes. Over generations, dark fur becomes more common.
content.explanationOnWrong: Dark mice are harder to catch, so they survive and reproduce more. Their genes spread through the population - natural selection!

content.question: What did Charles Darwin call the process where the best-adapted individuals survive?
content.hint: Darwin's key insight about how species change over time...
content.explanationOnCorrect: Natural selection! It's 'natural' because nature selects which traits help survival - no one plans it, it just happens.
content.explanationOnWrong: Darwin called it 'natural selection' - nature 'selects' the best-adapted individuals to survive and reproduce.

content.title: Genetics: Dominant and Recessive Traits
content.explanation: You have two copies of each gene - one from each parent. Some genes are dominant (they show up even with one copy). Others are recessive (both copies needed to show). Brown eyes are dominant over blue eyes - that's why two brown-eyed parents can still have a blue-eyed child!
content.visualAlt: Punnett square showing eye color genetics
keyPoints: Genes come in pairs (alleles)
Dominant alleles show their trait with just ONE copy
Recessive alleles need TWO copies to show
Capital = dominant (B), lowercase = recessive (b)
Bb = brown eyes (dominant wins); bb = blue eyes

content.question: A child has genotype 'Bb' for hair color (B = brown, dominant; b = blonde, recessive). What hair color do they have?
content.hint: They have one dominant allele (B). Dominant means it shows up with just one copy.
content.explanationOnCorrect: Brown! The dominant B allele overrides the recessive b. Just one copy of B is enough to show brown hair.
content.explanationOnWrong: With genotype Bb, the dominant B allele takes effect. Brown is dominant, so they have brown hair.

content.question: Which describes how two brown-eyed parents (each carrying one blue eye gene) can have a blue-eyed child?
options: Each parent passes their recessive 'b' allele, giving the child 'bb'
The child gets new genes from the environment
Blue eyes are dominant over brown
correct: Each parent passes their recessive 'b' allele, giving the child 'bb'
content.hint: Each parent is Bb. What happens if both pass their 'b' allele to their child?
content.explanationOnCorrect: Yes! If both Bb parents pass their 'b' allele, the child gets 'bb' (recessive from both sides) = blue eyes!
content.explanationOnWrong: Both parents are Bb. If the child inherits 'b' from each parent, they get 'bb' = blue eyes. There's a 25% chance of this!
